title: Kernels of homomorphisms with multiplicative-type source
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring, put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and use $S$-group schemes and homomorphisms in the sense of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Let $D\to S$ be of multiplicative type of finite presentation: locally for fppf coverings [def-pc-fppf-site], $D$ is isomorphic to $D_U(M)=\operatorname{Spec}_U\mathcal O_U[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, with group-algebra Hopf operations as in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Let $J\to S$ be any affine group scheme of finite presentation and let $u:D\to J$ be a group homomorphism. Define the scheme-theoretic kernel $N=D\times_{J,u,e_J}S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with its induced group operations. Then $N\hookrightarrow D$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $N$ is itself of multiplicative type of finite presentation over $S$. In particular $N\to S$ is affine, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented. Kernel formation and its inclusion in $D$ commute with every base change $A\to A'$. No smoothness or connectedness of $D,J,N$, no Noetherian or reducedness assumption on $A$, and no finiteness of the fibres of $N$ are required.

source.place: Conrad, Exercise 2.4.3(i)--(iii), printed p.76; finite-presentation version of the kernel assertion, using the local character argument and Corollary B.3.5, printed p.292. Read online; WANTED local archive as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this structural group-scheme result.

proof.text: First, kernel formation commutes with every base change, including the inclusion: both iterated fibre products represent pairs consisting of a point of the base-changed $D$ and an equality of its image with the identity. Their universal properties give mutually inverse maps preserving the projections and group operations. Since $J$ is affine over the affine $S$, write $J=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Its identity corresponds to an augmentation $\epsilon:B\to A$ split by the structure map, hence is a closed immersion. Its pullback is $N\hookrightarrow D$, which is therefore closed.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.3(ii), printed p.76; fibre-product universal property and Stacks 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion)

proof.text:
We shall work fppf locally with $D=D_A(M)$. Here the kernel is affine and finitely presented over $A$. Indeed choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ of $B$. Its augmentation ideal is generated by $b_i-\epsilon(b_i)$: subtracting the augmentation of a polynomial in the generators expresses it as a sum of multiples of these differences. Consequently
$$\mathcal O(N)=A[M]/(u^*(b_i)-\epsilon(b_i):1\le i\le t).$$
The subgroup-algebra presentation with subgroup $0\subseteq M$ makes $A[M]$ finitely presented over $A$, since $M$ is finitely generated. Adding the displayed finite list of relations preserves finite presentation. This calculation also applies to every split kernel used below.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.3(i),(ii), printed p.76; affine finite-presentation calculation

proof.text: For a split source we may reduce the affine group diagram to a Noetherian base. Write a finite presentation $B=A[X_1,\ldots,X_t]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$. Take the subring $R_0\subseteq A$ generated over $\mathbf Z$ by its finitely many coefficients and put $B_0=R_0[X_1,\ldots,X_t]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$. Tensoring this presentation identifies $B_0\otimes_{R_0}A$ with $B$. Enlarge $R_0$ through its finitely generated intermediate subrings in $A$. These rings are finite type over $\mathbf Z$ and their union is $A$. They are Noetherian: every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is generated by its least positive element, and apply the PID and finite-type permanence lemmas. Model $D(M)$ by the same group algebra and model finite products by tensor products. All objects are affine of finite presentation. The affine-limit lemma identifies their limits with their base changes to $A$. Apply finite-diagram descent to multiplication, identity, inverse, $u$, and the finitely many group and homomorphism identities, including the product projection identities. The lemma fixes only the model objects, not the descended projections. The pair of descended projections $V_{J\times J}\to V_J\times V_J$ (likewise for the triple product and for $D\times D$) is a morphism of finitely presented affine schemes, hence locally of finite presentation by the map-over-base lemma, and becomes the canonical product identification over $A$; isomorphism descent makes it an isomorphism after a further enlargement. This gives an affine finitely presented group $J_0$, a homomorphism $D_{A_0}(M)\to J_0$ and their specified base changes over $A$. Thus proving the split assertion over arbitrary Noetherian rings suffices; local diagonalizations pull back to local diagonalizations.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.3(i), printed p.76; Stacks 01ZM (finite diagrams), 01YW/01YX (affine limits), 00FN (Noetherian permanence)

proof.text: We now prove the local Noetherian case, writing $(A,\mathfrak m)$ for the base and $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Write $k[N_k]=k[M]/I$ using Step 2. The images $g_m$ of the $e_m$ are group-like in this quotient coalgebra, since the closed immersion is a group homomorphism. Put $L=\{m:g_m=1\}$. The Hopf formulas show this is a subgroup and $g_m=g_n$ exactly when $m-n\in L$. The quotient is spanned by the $g_m$, and its distinct group-like elements are linearly independent by the cited coalgebra lemma. Hence the map $k[M/L]\to k[N_k]$ sending $e_{\bar m}$ to $g_m$ is a bijective Hopf map. In particular the actual closed subgroup $N_k\subseteq D_k(M)$ is $D_k(M/L)$ with the quotient-character inclusion. This argument works over $k$ itself, without an algebraic-closure or reducedness hypothesis.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.1 and 2.4.3(ii), printed p.76; Hopf/group-like proof of the field subgroup description

proof.text:
Set $H=D_A(M/L)$ with its canonical inclusion into $D_A(M)$. The restricted homomorphism $w:H\to J$ has trivial special fibre by Step 4. For every $n\ge1$, the ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^n$ of $A/\mathfrak m^n$ is nilpotent, so diagonalizable nilpotent triviality gives $w\bmod\mathfrak m^n=1$. For $b\in B$, write the finite group-algebra expansion
$$w^*(b)-\epsilon(b)=\sum_{c\in M/L}a_c e_c.$$
Its reduction is zero for every $n$, so each $a_c\in\bigcap_n\mathfrak m^n$. Krull intersection, applied to the finite $A$-module $A$ and its Jacobson ideal $\mathfrak m$, gives $a_c=0$. Thus $w=1$ and $H\subseteq N$ scheme-theoretically. We used Krull intersection coefficient by coefficient, never for the generally infinite $A$-module $A[M/L]$, and never used smoothness of $J$.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.3(ii), printed p.76; Corollary B.2.7, printed p.287; Stacks 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module)(2)

proof.text:
The subgroup $L$ is finitely generated: regard $M$ as a finite $\mathbf Z$-module and apply the Noetherian-submodule lemma, using that $\mathbf Z$ is a PID. The relative character-duality lemma gives a faithfully flat finitely presented quotient
$$q:D_A(M)\longrightarrow D_A(L),\qquad\ker q=H.$$
The homomorphism $u$ descends to $v:D_A(L)\to J$. Explicitly, two lifts along $q$ differ by $H$, so their $u$-images agree because $u|_H=1$. This equality holds on the fibre product, as $D_A(M)\times_{D_A(L)}D_A(M)\simeq D_A(M)\times H$ via $(x,h)\mapsto(x,xh)$. Representable fpqc descent therefore constructs a unique scheme map $v$; the group identities are checked after the same cover on each input and follow from those of $u$. The quotient is an fppf cover by its stated flatness, finite presentation and sheaf-quotient description, and is fpqc by the cited covering lemma.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.3(iii), printed p.76; Appendix B.1 quotient by characters; Stacks 00IK and fpqc representable descent

proof.text: Let $K=\ker v$. The quotient description commutes with base change. For any $k$-scheme $T$ and any $z\in K_k(T)$, fppf locally lift $z$ along $q_k$ to $x\in D_k(M)$. Then $u_k(x)=v_k(z)=1$, so Step 4 gives $x\in H_k$, and hence $z=q_k(x)=1$. Equality with the identity descends because representable functors are fpqc sheaves. Thus $K_k=1_k$ as a scheme, including its infinitesimal structure. Choose finitely many generators of $L$, giving a surjection $\mathbf Z^r\twoheadrightarrow L$. Relative character duality embeds $D_A(L)$ as a closed subgroup of $D_A(\mathbf Z^r)=\mathbf G_m^r$. The kernel $K$ is closed by Step 1, so its composite inclusion into this torus is closed as well. The local-torus-subgroup lemma now gives $K=1_S$. Its hypotheses require only the Noetherian local base and the trivial special fibre; no flatness of $K$ is needed.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.3(iii), printed p.76; existing trivial-special-fibre torus-subgroup criterion

proof.text: Since $u=vq$ and $\ker v=1$, a point $x$ over any $A$-scheme lies in $\ker u$ exactly when $q(x)=1$. By the kernel formula for $q$ this says $N=H=D_A(M/L)$ as closed subgroup functors and therefore as group schemes with their specified inclusions. This proves the local Noetherian assertion. The zero group $M/L$ gives the trivial kernel, whereas $L=0$ gives the entire source; neither case was excluded.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.3(ii),(iii), printed p.76, assembly of the local kernel calculation

proof.text: Return to a Noetherian ring $A$ with split source, and fix $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its localization is Noetherian by the localization lemma, so Steps 4--8 give $N_{A_{\mathfrak p}}=D_{A_{\mathfrak p}}(M/L)$ for some subgroup $L\subseteq M$. Define $H=D_A(M/L)$ over $A$. The finitely many generator images of the coordinate map of $u|_H$ equal their augmentations after localization at $\mathfrak p$. Each difference has finite support in $A[M/L]$, so there exists $f\notin\mathfrak p$ killing all their finitely many coefficients. Therefore $u|_{H_{A_f}}=1$, giving $h:H_{A_f}\to N_{A_f}$. Both schemes are affine of finite presentation by Step 2 and the subgroup-algebra presentation; the map $h$ is locally of finite presentation by the map-over-base lemma. The inverse system of principal neighborhoods of $\mathfrak p$ inside $\operatorname{Spec}A_f$ has affine transitions and limit $\operatorname{Spec}A_{\mathfrak p}$. Its limit map $h_{A_{\mathfrak p}}$ is an isomorphism by Step 8. Isomorphism descent along this small directed system gives a further principal neighborhood where $h$ is an isomorphism. Thus $N$ is Zariski locally diagonalizable, not merely diagonalizable on its fibres.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.3(i), printed p.76, spreading the local answer; Stacks 00FN, 02FV, 01YW/01YX, 081E

proof.text: The Noetherian model of Step 3 and base-change identity of Step 1 now prove that for any ring $A$ a split-source kernel is Zariski locally $D(M/L)$. Indeed pull back the open cover and its group isomorphisms from the Noetherian model. Apply this on affine refinements of the given fppf splitting cover of the original $D$. Zariski covers are fppf, and fppf covers compose, so these diagonalizations form an fppf cover of the original $S$. Their character groups are finitely generated quotients of the finite $M$. This is precisely the multiplicative-type condition in the statement.

source.place: Exercise 2.4.3(i)--(iii), printed p.76; fppf locality and composition of covering families

proof.text: For completeness, the local diagonalizable models have the promised geometric properties. Their group algebras are free on the character group. For an injection $V\hookrightarrow W$ of modules, tensoring with this free algebra is the direct sum of copies of that injection, indexed by the basis, and is injective coordinate by coordinate. Thus the ring maps are flat by definition and the corresponding affine morphisms are flat by the affine criterion. The subgroup-algebra presentation with subgroup $0$ gives finite presentation for each finitely generated character group. Convert the fppf diagonalization cover to an fpqc cover. Affineness, flatness and local finite presentation descend by their respective cited lemmas. In particular $N$ is affine over the affine $S$, hence is affine and qcqs; the qcqs permanence lemma upgrades local finite presentation to finite presentation. This proves every asserted property. The entire argument allowed torsion characters and arbitrary base changes, including the empty scheme after base change to the zero ring.

source.place: Appendix B.1 diagonalizable models; Stacks 01U5, 02L5, 02L2, 02KY and finite-presentation qcqs criterion
